main_body: A bare, gnarled dead tree: a thick trunk with a flared root base and branches spreading above, with no leaf canopy.
top_band: none. The trunk is a vertical organic form with no horizontal top surface. The column reads from dark brown trunk down to a root flare at the base.
evidence: The subject is an organic tree, drawn as a trunk and branches seen from the front. An organic object has no required top surface, so the 3/4 top-and-front structure does not apply. There is no isometric side face and no flat panel or slab. The trunk is modelled with a lit left side and a dark right side, and the root base spreads at the bottom. The kind label matches. This is a plausible organic form, so it passes.

style.evidence: The reference trees are full leafy canopies with 5-6 greens, per-clump highlights and a shaded trunk. The candidate is a bare dead tree with about 4 brown steps: light tan highlights, mid brown, dark brown and a near-black deep tone. The outlines are tinted dark brown rather than neutral black. Some bark texture and a few green moss dots appear on the trunk, and there is a knothole. The branches are thin, 2-3px wide, and many tiles hold only 2-4 colours. The trunk has no bark grain across its wider areas. The piece is clean and craft-aware, but it is thinner and less richly textured than the reference trees. It has no canopy, so it is a weaker match for the kind, and it falls short of the reference standard.
